evidence.locator: zhsh/src/monster.js Monster constructor and assault victory settlement
evidence.finding: The surviving source calculates experience as monster level multiplied by 2. This produces tens of thousands of low-level encounters against the imported cumulative level thresholds and is rejected as a formal compatibility rule.

The independent implementation reads exp_reward and money_reward_min/max from each monster record, proving rewards need not be derived from the level-times-2 formula. Exact populated values are not present in that repository.
Nearby level-appropriate monsters and instances close ordinary level gates in a reasonable number of encounters; thousands of encounters are abnormal.

experience.derivation: A single continuous level gradient is fitted to the formal cumulative thresholds and task reward scale. Encounter-type multipliers follow the source monster-type difficulty ordering; no task, series, city, or level receives a special multiplier.
experience.replacement_condition: Replace when an authoritative populated monster reward table or an unambiguous original reward formula is recovered and validated jointly against the original level thresholds and task rewards.
